issues: The tiles were 25 grey-blue gradient cards with no poster content; once assembled they formed an even grey-blue grid, so nothing actually took shape
The only text was a small, widely tracked serif REASSEMBLE that read like a placeholder, leaving nothing worth reading in the hold
Tiles had no thickness or lighting; tumbling was just flat distortion, so the shards felt weightless
After the explosion the frame was simply empty: the last frame was a blank dark background with no landing
changes: Graphite look (near-monochrome with warm gold accents): all 25 tiles slice one 1440x810 launch key visual, an eclipse with dark disc, gold-white rim, diamond-ring highlight and horizontal streak, plus a 150px serif wordmark "Mosaic"; the layout follows tile rows so seams never cut letters

Tiles are now 16px-thick solid slabs (front slice, back and four edges): face normals from the rotation matrix drive Lambert lighting, so edges flash warm gold as they tumble and shards deep in z stay darker

Assembly flies in from z -300 to -1800 in a Manhattan ripple at 6.5f per ring, with bezier(0.33,0,0.15,1) for a fast flight, a long settle and a small seating wobble; as the last tile lands the rim lights up, the diamond ring flashes, the wordmark rises letter by letter, and one sheen crosses during the hold
Explosion: the centre goes first, each tile flies outward, toward camera and tumbles hard on EASE.exit; motion blur rises to 10 samples for this segment to avoid stepped ghosting
Once the shards clear, an end card sits underneath (gold ring mark, 140px wordmark, AVAILABLE OCTOBER 14), so the last frame is a complete poster; duration 156 to 180f
